sections.h2: Where is Jeff Davis County and what is its economy built on?
sections.html:
Jeff Davis County lies in southeast Georgia, with Hazlehurst as its seat and largest city and Denton as the only other city. The General Assembly created it on August 18, 1905, and it covers 335 square miles, 331 of them land, per Wikipedia.

Farming drives the local economy. Cotton and peanuts are the main crops, tobacco was once larger, and timber remains an important product. The county touches Wheeler, Montgomery, Toombs, Appling, Bacon, Coffee and Telfair counties. Water runs several ways here: the north and part of the west edge drain to the Lower Ocmulgee, the eastern corner to the Altamaha, and the south toward the Little Satilla and Satilla rivers.

Satilla is a census-designated place, and Roper, Snipesville and Tallahassee are unincorporated communities. That pattern of small towns and farm tracts shapes what sells: a house in Hazlehurst, a country place near a crossroads and a field with timber on it each draw a different buyer.

sections.h2: What do QuickFacts show about housing in Jeff Davis County?
sections.html:
Housing here is modest in price and thin in new construction. The Census Bureau lists a median owner-occupied value of $118,300 and an owner rate of 71.3% for 2020-2024.

The population peaked at 15,068 in 2010, slipped to 14,779 in 2020 and is estimated at 3.0% above that now. In the 2020 census, 33.1% of occupied homes were rented and the rental vacancy rate was 9.4%, so landlords here compete for tenants. Only nine permits in 2025 means few new homes are coming onto the market, and a seller's competition is mostly other older houses.

sections.h2: Where do I pay and ask questions about Jeff Davis County property tax?
sections.html:
Go to the Tax Commissioner at 14 Jeff Davis Street, Suite 104, Hazlehurst, GA 31539, or call (912) 375-6622. The office is open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the mailing address is PO Box 558.

  • Tax Commissioner: bills, collects, issues mobile home decals, and also collects timber tax, heavy duty equipment tax and intangible tax
  • Tax Assessor: sets values and handles appeals; phone (912) 375-6624
  • Board of Equalization: appointed by the Grand Jury, hears assessment appeals
  • County Commission and Board of Education: adopt the millage rates

A county payment page on a government portal also takes online payments, so ask the office which method suits you before you mail a check.

sections.h2: When is Jeff Davis County property tax due, and what are the penalties?
sections.html:
Bills are normally mailed by October 20, and payment is due by December 20 of the same year. Partial payments are accepted along the way.

After December 20, interest is added each month at the bank prime rate. On top of that, a 5% penalty is added every 120 days, until penalties reach 20%. A balance that sits for a year therefore climbs quickly, and the longer a payoff request is delayed the larger the figure at closing.

  • Mobile homes: bills usually go out in January and are due April 1; a current decal must be displayed
  • Mobile home penalty after the due date: 10% plus 1% a month, then a FiFa on the clerk's docket and possible auction of the home
  • Homesteaded mobile homes are taxed like real property when the owner also owns the land

One county page also mentions May 1 for mobile homes, so confirm that date with the office before relying on either.

sections.h2: What homestead and special assessment options does Jeff Davis County offer?
sections.html:
The standard homestead exemption is $2,000, taken off the 40% assessed value. It applies to county and school taxes, with carve-outs for municipal school levies and bond debt.

File at the Tax Commissioner's office, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays, between January 1 and April 1. The county says Georgia law gives no extension, so missing the date waives the exemption for that year. Once approved, it renews automatically until eligibility changes, and no exemption can exceed the tax owed. Where a local exemption exceeds the State's, the local one supersedes it.

  • Conservation use and residential transitional property (O.C.G.A. 48-5-7.4)
  • Agricultural preferential assessment (O.C.G.A. 48-5-7.4.1)
  • Rehabilitated historic property (O.C.G.A. 48-5-7.2)

Each of these three programs requires a covenant with the Tax Assessor to keep the property in its qualifying use for at least 10 years. Call (912) 375-6624 before you sell land enrolled in one, because the covenant can affect what a buyer inherits.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Jeff Davis County assessment?
sections.html:
Send a written appeal to the Board of Tax Assessors within 45 days of the notice date. Assessment notices usually go out in the spring, and the appeal must say which method you choose.

The grounds are taxability, value, uniformity or denial of an exemption. A dispute about the tax rate or the bill amount does not fit those grounds. Owners can also file a return between January 1 and April 1 stating what they think the property was worth on January 1, which sets up appeal rights if the assessors change it. Mobile home owners get 45 days from the day bills are mailed, then 21 days after a change notice to reach the Board of Equalization.

sections.h2: What should I do about tax when selling a Jeff Davis County house?
sections.html:
Ask the Tax Commissioner for a written payoff and have the closing office pay it from your proceeds. Interest and penalties accrue monthly and every 120 days, so a figure from a prior month may be short.

For land with timber on it, ask whether timber tax applies, since that bill is collected by the same office. If you own a mobile home on rented land, check the decal and the April 1 bill before you list it. A FiFa on the clerk's docket is a public record, and a buyer's title search will find it.

faqs.q: What is the Jeff Davis County property tax due date?
faqs.a: December 20. Bills normally go out by October 20, and partial payments are accepted before the deadline.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Jeff Davis County tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the Tax Commissioner at (912) 375-6622, at 14 Jeff Davis Street, Suite 104, in Hazlehurst. Valuation questions go to the Tax Assessor at (912) 375-6624.

faqs.q: What penalty applies to late Jeff Davis County taxes?
faqs.a: Interest accrues monthly at the bank prime rate, and a 5% penalty is added every 120 days up to 20%. Mobile homes pay 10% plus 1% a month after April 1.

faqs.q: How long do I have to file a Jeff Davis County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: You can file from January 1 through April 1 for the current tax year. The county says Georgia law allows no extension.

faqs.q: How long is the appeal window in Jeff Davis County?
faqs.a: It is 45 days from the date of the assessment notice. File the written appeal with the Board of Tax Assessors and state your chosen appeal method.
